NICHESv2

NICHESv2 scores ligand-receptor (LR) signaling between individual pairs of cells in spatial and non-spatial single-cell transcriptomics data. It keeps every non-zero score, so you can trace a signal back to the cells that produced it, and summarize signals by neighborhood when you need a wider view.

Installation

NICHESv2 is being prepared for CRAN. Until it is released there, install it from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RaredonLab/NICHESv2", ref = "main")

To read the vignette locally, add build_vignettes = TRUE, which needs knitr, rmarkdown and pandoc.

These packages are optional. Install only the ones you need:

# Seurat V4 and V5 objects
install.packages("SeuratObject")

# AnnData (.h5ad) files, no Python required
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("rhdf5")

# OmniPath LR database
BiocManager::install("OmnipathR")

# TissuePlex export
install.packages("arrow")

# Cell segmentation polygons
install.packages("sf")

Quick start

This example uses the small synthetic dataset that ships with the package.

library(NICHESv2)

data(NICHESv2_inputs)

# Score LR pairs between mutual spatial neighbors
obj <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data,
  LRM.db    = NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db,
  mode      = "spatial",
  k         = 5L
)

# One row per non-zero (edge, LR pair) score
head(obj$edge.data)

# Summarize each cell's neighborhood
obj <- aggregate_NICHESObject(obj, cell.type.col = "celltype")
head(obj$aggregations$neighborhood.edge.agg)
head(obj$aggregations$neighborhood.composition)

For your own data, pass a database name to LRM.db and set species:

obj <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx = count.mtx,
  meta.data = meta.data,
  LRM.db    = "connectomedb2025",
  species   = "mouse",
  mode      = "spatial",
  k         = 6L,
  n.cores   = 4L
)

The vignette walks through the full workflow:

vignette("NICHESv2")

The website has tutorials on public spatial and non-spatial datasets, plus a page for reviewers.

Features

  • Two analysis modes: "spatial" connects cells by k-nearest neighbors or a fixed radius, and adds autocrine self-loops. "nonspatial" pairs cells by random sampling within each pair of cell types.
  • LR databases: ConnectomeDB2025 and FANTOM5 are bundled for human, mouse, rat and pig, with no internet needed. OmniPath covers human, mouse and rat. You can also supply your own data frame, and multi-gene complexes are supported.
  • Memory-efficient storage: the 15-slot NICHESObject stores scores in sparse long-format data.tables, so memory use follows how much signal exists rather than every possible combination.
  • Neighborhood aggregation: aggregate_NICHESObject() gives directional scores per cell and LR pair (in, out, cross, self-autocrine and other-autocrine) and the cell-type makeup of each neighborhood.
  • Multiple samples: sample.col processes each sample separately and merges the results, so no edges cross samples.
  • Flexible input: use a sparse matrix, a Seurat V4 or V5 object, or an AnnData file (no Python required).
  • Works on every platform: parallel scoring uses socket clusters through n.cores.
  • Interactive viewing: export_to_TissuePlex() writes edges to a Parquet file for viewing in TissuePlex.

Citation

A paper describing NICHESv2 is in preparation. Until it is published, please cite the original NICHES method:

Raredon MSB, Yang J, Kothapalli N, et al. Comprehensive visualization of cell-cell interactions in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with NICHES. Bioinformatics. 2023;39(1):btac775. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btac775
